brief: Goldman's FICC and Equities desk previews its Communacopia and Technology conference, running Sep 8-11 in San Francisco with 260+ companies presenting, 2,160+ registered institutional investors and 31,700+ meeting requests, each above 2025. The desk frames the event against a damaged AI trade: in July and August its Software vs. Semis pair (GSPUSOSE) rallied more than 50% while its AI vs. AI-at-Risk pair (GSPUARTI) fell 48% peak to trough. It asks whether conference season is the catalyst that repairs the trade, and says the input it is watching is not AI adoption commentary but compute pricing, where investors disagree on the direction of spot and contracted markets beyond 2026, to be read off SPCX, neoclouds, hyperscalers and AKAM/DOCN. Its trade follows from crowding rather than fundamentals: engagement concentrates in already widely owned names, historically the 10 most in-demand tech stocks have outperformed SPXXAI and GSXUTECH in the week after the conference starts, so the desk expresses it via the equally weighted GSCBTC10 basket, delta one or 30Sep 105 115% call spreads at 1.68%. Positioning data shows software off its lows, semis rangebound, and August net inflows to Mag7.
